title: Free energy of Ising models under a spectral condition
abstract: A sequence of sparse weighted graphs $(G_N:N\ge 1)$ indexed by the number of vertices $N$ is said to be left-convergent if all (suitably weighted) subgraph counts converge to a limit as $N\to\infty$. This notion generalizes in a natural way Benjamini-Schramm's definition of local weak convergence. A broad research agenda aims at determining which `global' graph properties are determined by left or local weak convergence (in other words, which of these properties are in fact local). We prove that, under a spectral condition on the weighted adjacency matrix ${\boldsymbol A}_N$ of graph $G_N$, the free energy density of the Ising model on this weighted graph is continuous in the left convergence topology (and hence is a local function). Our proof uses the decomposition of the Ising measure as a log-concave combination of product measures, and of the rapid mixing of Langevin dynamics for log-concave measures. As applications, we derive new limit theorems for the free energy density of spin glasses, antiferromagnets, and magnetization constrained ferromagnetic models, on locally tree-like graphs.
summary: This paper rigorously proves that for Ising models defined on sequences of weighted graphs, the free energy density remains stable (continuous) under a specific type of graph convergence called left convergence. This breakthrough relies on imposing a spectral condition on the graph's adjacency matrix and uses advanced techniques involving log-concavity and Langevin dynamics.
main_problem: The central problem is determining which 'global' graph properties of an Ising model are determined by local weak convergence when the underlying graph structure converges in a specific sense.
main_result: Under a spectral condition on the weighted adjacency matrix and sparsity assumptions, the free energy density of the Ising model is proven to be continuous with respect to the left convergence topology.
method: The proof utilizes decomposing the Ising measure into log-concave combinations of product measures and leveraging the rapid mixing properties of Langevin dynamics for such measures.

key_observables: The normalized free energy density, $F(G) =  rac{1}{N} \log Z(G)$, is the primary observable.
important_parameters: Spectral properties of the adjacency matrix (eigenvalues lying in an interval $I$ with $|I|<1$), graph sparsity ($\|A\|_{\infty}$ bounded), and external field strength ($h$).
main_assumptions: The core result requires a spectral condition on $A_N$ and that the sequence of graphs must be sparse. The continuity proof relies on log-concavity and rapid mixing.

It then proves continuity of the free energy density under spectral conditions using advanced tools from stochastic processes (Langevin dynamics) before deriving explicit limit theorems for various disordered models.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical framework connecting local graph structure convergence to global thermodynamic quantities is highly relevant to understanding complex systems modeled by neural networks or random graphs in quantum information theory.
